title: The Cloth-Washer and the Imperial Messenger
summary: An arrogant imperial messenger rode his lathered horse into the drying meadow of an honest cloth-washer in Damascus, shouting that he must have fresh horses and dry boots immedi...
keywords: the fuller his wife and the trooper
full_text:
An arrogant imperial messenger rode his lathered horse into the drying meadow of an honest cloth-washer in Damascus, shouting that he must have fresh horses and dry boots immediately, threatening to burn the laundry if he was delayed.

The cloth-washer’s wife stepped forward with a charming, deferential bow: 'O mighty courier! Enter our warm laundry room, sit by the charcoal drying stove, and drink this bowl of hot spiced cordial while my husband grooms your horse!'

The tired courier swallowed the spiced cordial, which was steeped with mild wild poppy syrup. Within ten minutes, he was snoring peacefully upon the soft pile of clean carpets!

The cloth-washer groomed the horse, fed the animal fresh barley, and when the courier awoke two hours later fully rested, the horse was ready, the boots were polished, and the courier’s frantic anger was completely dissolved!

The courier thanked them with five silver dirhams, having learned that a hot drink and an hour of rest conquer haste faster than a whip.
moral: Presence of mind and good humor defuse arrogance without violence.
